question: A 57-year-old man presents to his family physician for a routine exam. He feels well and reports no new complaints since his visit last year. Last year, he had a colonoscopy which showed no polyps, a low dose chest computerized tomography (CT) scan that showed no masses, and routine labs which showed a fasting glucose of 93 mg/dL. He is relatively sedentary and has a body mass index (BMI) of 24 kg/m^2. He has a history of using methamphetamines, alcohol (4-5 drinks per day since age 30), and tobacco (1 pack per day since age 18), but he joined Alcoholics Anonymous and has been in recovery, not using any of these for the past 7 years. Which of the following is indicated at this time?
analysis: Given the patient's history of alcohol, tobacco, and methamphetamine use, along with his age and sedentary lifestyle, he is at increased risk for various health conditions, including liver disease, lung cancer, and cardiovascular disease. Considering his risk factors, a chest radiograph (option d) would be indicated at this time to screen for any potential lung abnormalities related to his past substance use.
